PullRequest.Title: chat: clarify customization migration guidance
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

## Summary

Make Customizations > Migrations more welcoming and explain why migration is needed without turning the introduction into technical documentation.

- Heading: **Keep your customizations working**.
- Introduction: "Copilot's new agent runtime uses different formats and locations for some customizations. Review and migrate the affected items below."
- Add **Learn About Migrations**, linking to https://aka.ms/vscode-migrate-customizations.
- Move agent-specific guidance into the **Migrate with Agent** tooltip and accessible description: "Open a new chat with an agent to review and migrate your customizations. This uses Copilot credits."
- Make manual-review guidance point to the actual **Review** button.
- Use "Your customizations are ready." in the completed state, retaining "No migrations are needed."
- Update accessibility help and tests for copy, tooltips, link activation, and focus restoration. Move the existing unsupported-harness test out of a nested test so it executes as intended.

Navigation labels, category terminology, conversion warnings, and migration execution remain unchanged.

Related follow-up: #342218 tracks source-to-target group headers and consistent terminology across related surfaces. This PR does **not** implement or close that issue.

## Review and validation

Reviewed all three changed files; no actionable findings remain. Fast-forwarded the branch to current `main` before the final validation.

Commands below passed using the repository-required Node 24.18.0:

- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- npm.cmd run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed; client transpilation refreshed.
- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationDashboard.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, **15 tests**.
- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- npm.cmd run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationDashboard.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationAccessibility.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationDashboard.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm.cmd exec --yes --package=node@24.18.0 -- npm.cmd run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed before committing.

Smoke/integration suites and live screen-reader testing were not run locally. Screenshot CI investigation confirmed all 79 blocking hashes match; its failure was an unrelated image-hover fixture timeout, so no baseline changes were made.

## How to test

1. Open Customizations > Migrations with pending migrations for the Copilot runtime.
2. Check the new heading, shorter introduction, and Learn About Migrations link.
3. Activate the documentation link by mouse and keyboard; it should open the migration guide. Focus should remain usable after refreshing the overview.
4. Hover Migrate with Agent and verify that the tooltip explains the new-chat action and Copilot credit usage.
5. For a Needs manual review group, verify that its guidance points to Review and that Review still opens the item details.
6. With no pending or ignored migrations, verify the completed-state copy and absence of migration controls.
7. Open accessibility help and verify the documentation-link guidance and explicit Copilot-credit disclosure.



## Review follow-up

Fixed documentation-link focus loss when refreshing a completed overview, including refreshes through the loading state. The regression test failed before the fix and passes afterward. Initially completed overviews still do not take focus automatically.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the Customizations > Migrations dashboard, including loading-to-overview and completed-overview refreshes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing migration discovery completes before showOverview renders the dashboard. The diff adds one Link construction during render and, only when the previous documentation link held focus, one focus() call after the rebuilt overview is ready. Neither addition waits on migration discovery or adds asynchronous work to the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: computeMigration discovers customization migration candidates through the migration service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per enabled migration category after refresh coalescing; categories execute concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same category discovery calls and scheduling occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery must finish before the overview can be rendered; warm UI-only rerenders use already held results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: provideSourceFolders resolves destination folders for migration target types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct target type after Set deduplication, executing concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deduplicated target-folder resolution occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery waits for these calls before committing migration results; they are not invoked by Link rendering or focus restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing tree/model work scales with discovered migration candidates. Diff-added work remains O(1): one link, a fixed number of listeners, one map entry, and at most one focus call per overview render.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing refreshes are coalesced by customizationMigrationRefreshDelayer and stale work is cancellation/sequence guarded. Enabled migration categories and deduplicated target types are queried with Promise.all; the diff does not change this concurrency. Link creation and focus restoration are synchronous singleton operations per render.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Migration results remain in editor state and render from that state; refresh events are delayed/coalesced and stale requests are cancelled. The new Link has no cache and is disposed/recreated once per render via renderDisposables.clear(), so listeners and gesture targets do not accumulate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed render lines, Link implementation, disposal path, refresh call flow, coalescing, cancellation, and transitive service boundaries were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact migration discovery latency and candidate counts depend on harness and workspace, but those costs and their scheduling are unchanged. The added constant DOM work is negligible relative to existing full dashboard reconstruction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new render work is constant and cleaned up before each rebuild; focus restoration is conditional and occurs once after render.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate Learn About Migrations by mouse, keyboard, or touch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The opener boundary occurs only after explicit user activation. It is not reached while opening, rendering, laying out, or refreshing the dashboard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/opener/browser/link.ts:119 Link constructor activation handler, instantiated at src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigrationDashboard.ts:466
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the external migration documentation URL through IOpenerService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one opener call per click, Enter/Space activation, or tap event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no migration-documentation opener action on this dashboard before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User-requested navigation depends on the opener; dashboard rendering and migration workflows do not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales only with explicit user activations, not migration item count, refresh frequency, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each activation produces one openerService.open call. There is no loop or fan-out; aggregate concurrency is limited by user activations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved; any browser/network caching is outside this path. Failed or repeated activations are not automatically retried.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Link activation wiring and opener call were directly inspected, and tests establish one call per activation event.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External URL handling and network latency vary by environment, but they are intentional user-requested costs and do not block the dashboard.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly introduced boundary is the requested documentation action, has cardinality one, and is off the dashboard critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open accessibility help for customization migrations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible help content is assembled on demand by joining a fixed list of localized strings. The diff adds one fixed string and changes copy in another; no service or I/O is awaited.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The diff-added allocation is constant and independent of migration item count, workspace size, or session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous provider invocation per accessible-help request; no queue, fan-out, or background work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior. Content is generated on demand from a fixed-size list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete provider implementation and changed hunk were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the fixed additional text is small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra fixed string does not create realistic CPU, memory, serialization, or boundary cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all three changed files and every diff hunk. Traced dashboard render/refresh lifecycle, focus behavior, Link disposal and activation, migration discovery boundaries, coalescing/cancellation, effective concurrency, and accessible-help generation. No actionable performance finding or regression-fix learning signal was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
